summary: Paperboy entries from the prepared 1000-title candidate queue, researched for Sami's fidelity-first archive route.

entries.title: Paperboy
entries.definitive_edition: Original arcade cabinet; owned Midway arcade collection as practical capture fallback

emulation.emulator: Official collection/emulation route if cabinet is unavailable
emulation.notes: Document input-device mismatch if not using handlebar controls.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original arcade cabinet controls and display

primary.platform: Arcade cabinet / owned Midway arcade collection
primary.why: Paperboy's original arcade version used distinctive bicycle-handlebar controls, making cabinet or control-faithful preservation the authenticity target. Owned Midway arcade compilations are practical capture routes, but the original cabinet remains the control reference.
primary.how_to_play: Use an original cabinet when possible, or an owned Midway arcade collection for capture. Record route, input device, difficulty street, day reached, score, lives, collection/emulator settings, and whether NES/home ports were compared separately.

secondary.platform: Midway Arcade Treasures / Xbox Live Arcade / other owned compilations
secondary.what_to_play: Use if cabinet access is unavailable.
secondary.why: Collections are easier to capture but lose the original handlebar controls.

secondary.platform: NES / home computer / home console ports
secondary.why: The arcade version is the primary identity.

all_releases.fidelity: Original Atari Games cabinet with handlebar controls.

all_releases.platform: Midway arcade compilations / Xbox Live Arcade
all_releases.fidelity: Practical official arcade-emulation route when owned.
all_releases.reason: secondary: capture route, but not control-authentic.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Original cabinet controls are central; collection/emulation routes are practical but not control-authentic.

entries.remaster_caveats: Record input device and collection/emulator route; do not merge Paperboy 2 or Paperboy 64.
